chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
That ʿAlī عليه السلام administered the hadd punishment to a man who married a woman during her nifās before she had become pure.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Bābawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say regarding this hadith that he only administered the hadd punishment to him because he had had intercourse with her, because if he had not had intercourse with her, the hadd punishment would not have become obligatory upon her, since she had exited the ʿiddah by delivering what was in her womb. What he mentioned, may Allah have mercy on him, is possible if the woman was divorced. But if we suppose that she was one whose husband had died, then her delivering the pregnancy does not remove her from the ʿiddah; rather, she needs to complete the ʿiddah of four months and ten days. We have already clarified that in the Book of Marriage. If the matter is as we have mentioned, then Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام only administered the punishment to him because she had not yet exited the ʿiddah which is the ʿiddah of the woman whose husband has died. And both possibilities are plausible.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the widow’s waiting period of four months and ten days
key_terms.تَطْهُرَ: to become ritually pure from bleeding
key_terms.مُتَوَفًّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: a woman whose husband has died
key_terms.نِفَاسِهَا: her postnatal bleeding period after childbirth

ai.seo_question: Why was a man punished for marrying a woman during nifās before she became pure?
ai.summary: This report states that Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام punished a man who married a woman during her nifās before her purification. The accompanying discussion explains two possible legal understandings: either the punishment was due to intercourse after a marriage contracted following a completed post-divorce ʿiddah, or because the woman was still in the ʿiddah of widowhood, which continues for four months and ten days.
